Skip next section Saudi-led coalition command center hit by Houthi strike on Aden 10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 Saudi-led coalition command center hit by Houthi strike on Aden Fighting in Yemen has escalated since September [FILE October 2026] Image: Abdulnasser Alseddik/AP Photo/picture alliance A Houthi missile strike on Yemen's southern port city of Aden on Thursday targeted command centers of a Saudi-led coalition and Yemeni government forces, an unnamed government minister told AFP news agency several hours after the attack. Earlier reports said explosions were heard in the vicinity of the presidential palace in Aden, where Yemen's internationally-recognized government is based. Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani, and cabinet officials, were unharmed, adding the attack had been carried out with five missiles. Two members of the prime minister’s security detail were reported killed. Shorty after the attack, a Houthi-aligned television channel reported that a "military headquarters run by Saudi officers" was attacked. Aden has been the interim seat of Yemen's government since Houthi rebels based in the north took over the capital, Sanaa, and other parts of northern Yemen in 2014. A Saudi-led coalition is fighting the Iran-backed Houthis alongside government forces. Although Iran did not directly claim responsibility for the tanker fire, state television cited an army statement saying an "offending" and "non-compliant" tanker had switched off its tracking system while trying to pass thought "the prohibited zone." The US military, which is also enforcing a maritime blockade in the region, has not issued a statement. The reported incident comes a day after Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said a cargo vessel was sunk while passing through Strait of Hormuz after striking a mine. Iranian state media quoted the IRGC as saying the ship was sailing on an "unauthorized route," but did not share details of the vessel's identity or the fate of its crew. The state television report included footage of an unidentified ship listing and billowing a plume of smoke. Meanwhile, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said a Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride was hit by "unknown projectiles" on Tuesday and sank. US broadcaster CNN reported that the GFS Pride is the ship the IRGC claimed struck a mine, and cited expert assessment that a drone strike is likely what actually caused the sinking. How much oil is getting through the Strait of Hormuz? The MPA also reported a second vessel, the GFS Giselle, was attacked by projectiles on Tuesday, and sustained damage but was able to reach safe anchorage. "Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law," the authority said. The US military has not commented. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) reported Wednesday that two container ships were struck on Tuesday by projectiles but sustained only minor damage. According to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) , the GFS Pride is one of only two ships to have been sunk in the Strait of Hormuz out of 114 reported incidents since the US launched the war with Iran in February. https://p.dw.com/p/5OIok Skip next section Houthis target Yemen government palace in Aden 10/15/2026 October 15, 2026 Houthis target Yemen government palace in Aden Yemen's internationally-recognized government is located in Aden [FILE DECEMBER 2025] Image: Saleh Al-Obeidi/AFP On Thursday, Houthi rebels said a missile attack targeted the Yemeni government's interim capital, Aden. Witnesses cited by news agencies reported several explosions and smoke rising from the area around the al-Maashiq Palace following the rare attack on the headquarters of Yemen's internationally recognized government in the southern port city. Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani and members of the government were safe, according to Yemen's Information Ministry. The ministry statement added two members of the prime minister's security detail were killed. Other reports, citing government officials, said 10 people were injured. It is currently unclear if the palace itself was hit, or what the extent of damage could be. Houthi-affiliated media reported the strikes targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them." Houthi military spokesperson Yahya ​Saree said the strikes targeted what he called "Saudi ‌military operations headquarters in Aden," Reuters reported. Yemen's civil war reignited in September as the Iran-backed Houthis launched a rapid offensive against government forces, capturing key territory along the Red Sea coast and expanding their control over swathes of territory on the Red Sea. Since then both sides have regularly traded strikes . The Houthis have launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, with several killed in separate attacks on Riyadh airport . Despite, Saudi-led coalition airstrikes and government counter-offensives, the group’s recent territorial gains have largely remained intact. Can Yemen's government turn the tide against the Houthis? Photograph: Graham Turner/The Guardian Nottingham Nottinghamshire police officer in hospital after being shot in the foot Large cordon in place around Angel Row area of city centre after ‘shocking incident’ in the early hours of Sunday Josh Halliday North of England editor Sun 18 Oct 2026 05.32 EDT Last modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 05.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A police officer is in hospital after being shot in the foot in Nottingham in the early hours of Sunday. Nottinghamshire police said the officer had approached two suspects in the city centre when he was struck by a bullet. The force said the two suspects, a woman and a man, had fled the scene and were being sought by police. The firearm was recovered and a large crime scene is in place around Angel Row in the heart of the city after the incident at 4.50am. Claire Rukas, assistant chief constable, said: “This is a shocking incident and a sobering reminder of the potential dangers faced by officers as they work to protect and serve the public. “As we investigate what happened and work to apprehend the individuals involved, my thoughts today are with the injured officer, his family and colleagues. “I also ask that anyone with additional information shares this with us without delay. Even the smallest bit of information could make all the difference to this investigation.” A team of forensics experts were working within the police cordon on Sunday morning, sectioning off a large part of the city centre occupied by pubs, bars and takeaways. Curtis Jackson, 22, who said he had recently moved to the UK from the US, told the Nottingham Post he felt “quite worried to be in the city at night”. He said: “My thoughts go out to the police officer; this is really a terrible incident. It’s a scary thought that on a Saturday night, when most people go out to have a fun night, someone was in town with a gun ready to use it.” Another person, who gave her name only as Melissa, told the newspaper: “Incidents like this just amplify the feeling I have, I don’t feel safe in the city at all and when it’s dark any more. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion “I know police do all they can, but they can’t be everywhere and it feels like scary incidents are becoming all too common nowadays.” Explore more on these topics Nottingham England Police news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story ‘Instant connection to the past’: how the Major oak affected those who saw it ‘Most famous tree in the world’: Sherwood Forest’s 1,000-year-old Major oak dies ‘It’s a special tree’: campaign to save mother of beloved bramley apple for nation Nottingham paper takes legal action over Reform council’s ban on reporters ‘Free pint when Forest score!’: pub loses £1,500 after seven-goal rampage Brinsley Headstocks mining landmark to be reconstructed after public outcry Nottingham city council hits back at Sunak’s ‘letting down residents’ claims Nottingham city council plans cuts to libraries, care homes and youth services Nottingham city council issues notice in effect declaring itself bankrupt Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.bursa.ro/study-lack-of-money.text: Lack of financial resources and economic uncertainty are causing many Romanians to postpone important decisions, such as purchasing a home, starting a business, continuing their studies or changing their lifestyle. One third of those who have not yet taken concrete steps toward achieving their personal goals have been in this situation for at least three years, according to a survey conducted by Reveal Marketing Research for XTB Romania. The main obstacle to achieving these plans is a lack of money, cited by 43% of survey participants. Nearly one third of respondents say they must prioritize other expenses and responsibilities, while 30% prefer to postpone important decisions because of economic uncertainty. The survey data indicate a significant gap between Romanians' aspirations and the concrete measures taken to achieve them. Only approximately 20% of respondents have already begun implementing their plans or are actively working toward achieving their proposed goals. "For me, the concrete figure is that more than 7 in 10 Romanians have not taken concrete steps toward achieving their goal. In other words, we want something, but we have not yet started doing anything about it,” said Claudiu Cazacu, strategy consultant at XTB Romania. Ensuring family stability and security is the main concern for 45% of Romanians surveyed. Next come travel and important personal experiences, mentioned by 41% of respondents, and renovating or improving living conditions, at 40%. "Broadly speaking, the most important thing for Romanians is to ensure the security of their family's future, not just the present. We are living in increasingly interesting times, so it is natural that what we want is security. We need a refuge,” explained Claudiu Cazacu. At the same time, the study highlights Romanians' concern for the balance between professional and personal life. Thus, 34% of participants would like to reduce the time dedicated to work in favor of free time, while 31% intend to start a business or develop a personal project. More than a quarter of respondents include purchasing a home among their goals. Priorities differ, however, depending on age. In the 25-34 age category, 37% of respondents are interested in continuing their studies or acquiring new skills, while 30% are considering moving to another city or another country. By contrast, interest in entrepreneurship is higher among people over the age of 35. Approximately 38% of respondents in the 35-44 age category and 42% of those aged 45-55 say they want to develop their own business or a personal project. Across the entire sample, only 1% of participants say they have no personal goals. "In addition to this, according to the survey, experiences and travel, as well as home renovations, are very important to Romanians. For young people, specifically for 37% of respondents in the 25-34 age category, it is very important to continue their studies, have new experiences or move to another country. However, regardless of which country you are in, it is important to invest,” added Claudiu Cazacu. For her part, Irina Cristescu, General Manager of XTB Romania, believes that difficulties in achieving personal goals are not determined exclusively by income levels. "Romanians know what they want, but very many remain in the waiting stage for years. Beyond income levels, we are also talking about predictability, confidence and the ability to build a long-term plan. I believe that one of the most important financial challenges of the moment is to reduce the distance between "I would like to' and "I have started',” said Irina Cristescu. * Only 29% of Romanians Speak Openly About Their Future Plans Although most Romanians have long-term personal goals, few choose to discuss them openly. According to the survey, only 29% of respondents speak without reservations about their plans and aspirations, while 46% prefer to share them with only a few close people. Another 12% rarely discuss what they want to achieve, 8% almost never do, and 5% do not talk to anyone about their own goals. This reluctance is primarily explained by the personal nature of these aspirations, a reason cited by 44% of respondents. At the same time, 35% prefer not to reveal their intentions before having a concrete plan, while 23% avoid these discussions because they are unsure whether they have the necessary financial resources. Another 22% choose to talk about their goals only when they begin to materialize, while 20% admit that they fear possible failure. "As far as communication is concerned, only 29% of Romanians speak openly about their plans. 44% of people do not talk about their ideas until they have a concrete plan. These things are connected to the fact that when you talk about something that is not clearly defined, it is not something specific, and people make a choice that suits their personal profile. Some prefer to work in silence or not communicate. However, there are also people who do not communicate because they consider that their plans are still at the idea stage,” explained Claudiu Cazacu. Financial difficulties are also reflected in saving behavior. According to the survey, only 18% of Romanians regularly allocate money to savings or investments intended to achieve personal goals. A quarter of respondents save only occasionally, when their financial situation allows, while 24% say they currently lack the resources to put money aside. The differences between women and men are significant. Approximately 29% of women participating in the survey say they cannot afford to save for personal plans, compared with 18% of men. At the same time, the proportion of those who consistently save or invest is 21% among men and 16% among women. * Young People Are More Optimistic, but Many Do Not Know Where to Start Despite financial difficulties, nearly half of respondents believe they will manage to make progress toward achieving their personal goals over the next 12 months. The highest level of optimism is recorded among people aged between 25 and 34. Among the 18-24 age group, lack of experience and information represent additional obstacles. One in five young people in this category say they do not know what measures they should take to begin fulfilling their plans. Furthermore, 36% of respondents aged between 18 and 24 anticipate that, a decade from now, they might regret not having started investing earlier. This is also the most frequently anticipated category of financial regret across the entire sample. Representatives say that XTB data regarding the use of Investment Plans indicate growing interest among Romanians in investment instruments. Since the product's launch in 2023, tens of thousands of users in Romania have funded such a plan at least once, and their number has doubled within a year. "Starting in 2023, when the XTB "Investment Plans' product was implemented, if we are talking about a nominal figure, we can say that tens of thousands of Romanians have invested in these investment plans because they considered them a good start on their journey into the world of investments and, at the same time, an opportunity to create a much better structured and diversified portfolio,” said Radu Puiu, financial analyst at XTB Romania. According to the company, approximately 80% of people who started using the product still have an active plan. Two thirds of users are aged between 25 and 44. "From this point of view, we can say that 80% of those who started an investment plan still have it active even today, and this shows that the first step tends to be the hardest, namely the moment when we begin pursuing our goals and plans that we intend to put into practice,” explained Radu Puiu. The financial analyst also highlighted the rate of growth in the number of users, against a backdrop of interest in investments and access to financial information. "One in two current users joined in the last two months, which shows that, as people have become more informed and more educated about the world of investments, they have adopted this new product,” he added. According to Radu Puiu, the product's features, including the possibility of automating contributions, can simplify the investment process. "Investment plans change the dynamics because they offer a better structured and easier way to invest, considering the automation and other features they provide. The product was launched in Romania in 2023, so we have a three-year time horizon that we have analyzed,” the financial analyst specified. * Two in Ten Investors Start With Less Than 25 Euros The value of the initial investment varies considerably. Approximately 20% of users start with amounts of less than 25 euros, while 16% allocate more than 500 euros from the outset. Subsequently, one third of those who continue investing end up contributing larger amounts than those initially deposited. Radu Puiu believes that one of the main difficulties encountered by people who want to start investing is the perception that they would need substantial initial capital. "When we talk about the first step in investing, we automatically think about the amount with which we can start these investments. This is one of the aspects that creates many obstacles in making the decision to embark on this path, because people always think that perhaps the amount they have available is not sufficient, or they wonder what they could do with such a small amount or what an acceptable threshold for investments would be. These questions create a psychological barrier,” he explained. Data on initial investments show that most users choose to start with amounts of no more than 500 euros. "However, if we look at the results of investors who have accessed "Investment Plans', we see that two in ten started investing with less than 25 euros, which represents a considerably smaller amount than we might imagine at first glance when thinking about investments. Also, only 16% started investing with more than 500 euros. This shows us that more than 64% of investors started with an amount between 25 and 500 euros,” stated Radu Puiu. "If we look at the amounts generally involved in the world of investments, these could be considered quite small, which means that it is more important to start somewhere, regardless of the amount, and to have a plan,” added the financial analyst. Regarding preferred financial instruments, the most popular are exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that provide exposure to major American companies and international markets. These are followed by ETFs focused on technology and artificial intelligence, European markets and gold.
